name: Providenciales International Airport
before:
The main way into the Turks and Caicos, on the island of Providenciales. The territory is a British Overseas Territory, and this is one of two international airports, the other being JAGS McCartney on Grand Turk.

Note the name change. In 2023 the airport was renamed Howard Hamilton International, so both names are still in circulation and a client may see either on a ticket.

It handles more than 12,000 commercial aircraft movements a year, and the two local carriers, interCaribbean Airways and Caicos Express Airways, both run hubs here, which is how island hopping across the territory works.

There is one runway, 2,807 metres of asphalt, at an elevation of 15 feet. The runway extension and a terminal renovation were completed by December 2014.
after:
The main way into the Turks and Caicos, on the island of Providenciales. Nearly all international flights to this British Overseas Territory land here.

Note the name change. It was officially renamed Howard Hamilton International Airport in May 2024, but both names are in use and the code is still PLS.

The two local airlines, interCaribbean Airways and Caicos Express Airways, both have hubs here. Caicos Express flies daily to Grand Turk.

There is one runway, 2,807 metres of asphalt. The terminal was enlarged in 2014 and now runs well beyond the capacity it was designed for, so allow extra time, especially on Saturdays. A new arrivals hall, Terminal B, is being designed, with the building work still to be tendered.

claims.claim: one of two international airports, the other JAGS McCartney
claims.wasBefore: this is one of two international airports, the other being JAGS McCartney on Grand Turk
claims.why: Sources disagree on the count: Wikipedia says two, Visit TCI says three (with scheduled international flights only at Providenciales and South Caicos), and the operator lists four airports named International (Providenciales, Grand Turk, South Caicos, North Caicos). Replaced by the point both agree on, that nearly all international flights land here.

claims.claim: renamed in 2023

claims.why: The official renaming was on 21 May 2024. Corrected.

claims.why: No source on ticket wording. Replaced by the code, which is unchanged.

claims.claim: more than 12,000 commercial aircraft movements a year
claims.wasBefore: It handles more than 12,000 commercial aircraft movements a year
claims.why: Only Wikipedia and sites that copy it give the figure, undated. No operator or official traffic figure from the last 12 months was found.

claims.claim: island hopping works through these hubs
claims.wasBefore: which is how island hopping across the territory works
claims.why: No second source, and ferries also link the islands. Replaced by the daily Caicos Express flight to Grand Turk.

claims.claim: elevation of 15 feet
claims.why: Sources disagree: Wikipedia and OurAirports say 15 ft, the operator says 28 ft. Of no use to an agent, so cut rather than chosen.

claims.claim: runway extension and terminal renovation completed by December 2014
claims.wasBefore: The runway extension and a terminal renovation were completed by December 2014
claims.why: True but stale as a description of the airport today. The 2014 enlargement is kept; the rest is replaced by the current state (over capacity, Terminal B in design).

opinion.why: Signpost for the renaming sentence that follows; carries no fact of its own.
